name: Bear Pro
subcategory: notes, wikis and personal knowledge bases
tagline: Write tagged Markdown notes with backlinks and sync them across Apple devices

pricing.notes: Official monthly subscription in common USD storefronts.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Core local note-taking and free TXT, Markdown, TextBundle, Bear Note and RTF exports; no numeric note/storage cap published; 0 native cross-device sync

tiers.name: Bear Pro
tiers.limits: 1 subscription covers all devices on the same Apple ID; iCloud sync, encryption, OCR attachment search and advanced export

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free core app; no numeric note or storage cap is published; native cross-device sync requires Pro
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; both include a 7-day trial and auto-renew through Apple
pricing.hiddenCosts: Prices, taxes and refunds are controlled by Apple's storefront. Students and scholars can receive 30% off the first annual year, then renew at full price. Legacy subscribers keep the old price only while subscription continuity is maintained.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Bear Pro, write tagged Markdown notes with backlinks and sync them across Apple devices. The hard boundary is native apple polish, encrypted icloud sync, mobile capture, and typography, plus sync, collaboration, and capture polish.
coreLoopDIY: Write tagged Markdown notes with backlinks, search them instantly, sync across Apple devices, and export a normal Markdown folder.
requirements: optional sync folder chosen by the user
whatYouLose: native Apple polish, encrypted iCloud sync, mobile capture, and typography
ongoingBurden: file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Bear Pro because people keep paying when the note system is trusted across every device and disappears into their daily capture habits. The recurring cost buys file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Active open-source workspace with local-first documents and databases.

alternatives.name: FSNotes
alternatives.desc: Bear's tagged Markdown heart, minus the house style and subscription.

facts.install: Install the notarized macOS app or the iOS app; free GitHub builds are available alongside optional paid App Store copies
facts.dataFormat: User-chosen folders containing plain-text Markdown/RTF files, TextBundle packages, or AES-256 encrypted `.etp` bundles; optional iCloud Drive, Dropbox (macOS), or Git repositories sync those files
facts.gapVsPaid: It preserves the tagged plain-text idea, but Bear's editor, mobile polish, themes, and seamless first-party Apple sync are noticeably more refined.
facts.setupBlocker: The app installs cleanly, but reliable free cross-device use is Apple-centric and normally means choosing an iCloud Drive folder; iOS does not support Dropbox, WebDAV, or Google Drive sync

alternatives.name: Joplin
alternatives.desc: Tagged Markdown notes with real sync choices and rather less Apple polish.

facts.install: Install the native desktop/mobile app; then optionally choose Joplin Cloud, a third-party sync target, or a self-hosted Joplin Server
facts.engines: Optional desktop AI connects to Joplin Cloud AI, Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter, and vLLM; semantic search uses a downloaded local embedding model
facts.dataFormat: Each device keeps a local `database.sqlite` with notes, notebooks, tags, metadata, sync state, and encryption keys plus a `resources/` attachment directory; configured sync targets receive Joplin item records/resources, optionally end-to-end encrypted
facts.gapVsPaid: It is more portable and configurable, but its interface and editing experience feel less native and polished on Apple devices than Bear's.
facts.setupBlocker: The app itself installs cleanly, but free multi-device use requires choosing and correctly configuring a sync target; enabling E2EE must start on one device and the master-key password cannot be recovered

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.desc: Local Markdown, backlinks and a plugin bazaar; sync is still your problem.

facts.install: Install the native Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, or Android app; no account is required for local use
facts.dataFormat: Ordinary Markdown files and attachments in a user-chosen local vault folder, with app settings and plugins under `.obsidian`; optional paid Obsidian Sync stores end-to-end-encrypted replicas in Obsidian's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: The local Markdown core is excellent, but the free path does not include Bear-like first-party multi-device sync and the app demands more setup and decisions.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal local knowledge base DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Bear Pro in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and Markdown files as the source of truth; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: write tagged Markdown notes with backlinks, search them instantly, sync across Apple devices, and export a normal Markdown folder.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Store one Markdown file per note and a small SQLite index that can be rebuilt at any time.
Support wiki links, tags, backlinks, daily notes, pinned notes, and full-text search.
Add a fast command palette and keyboard-first create, rename, move, and link actions.
Render Markdown with task lists, code blocks, tables, and local image attachments.
Detect external file changes and show a safe conflict-resolution view.
Provide full-folder export, import, and an index-rebuild command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out proprietary sync servers.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer documents.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace and hosted public sites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
